problem_statement:
feat(schedule): unattended recurring runs via Task Scheduler/cron

New `wells schedule add/list/remove` subcommand plus a /schedule REPL
command (list/add/remove, add opens a TUI modal like /rules add) --
closes the "no cron/daemon mode" gap versus Claude Code's own
scheduled routines. Wells doesn't need to be running for a scheduled
run to fire; the OS scheduler invokes `wells` directly.

Interval spec: every<N>m / every<N>h / daily@HH:MM, or a raw 5-field
cron expression (Linux/macOS only -- Windows Task Scheduler has no
cron-expression concept, rejected there rather than mistranslated).

Each schedule gets a small wrapper script instead of trying to embed
the goal directly in a Task Scheduler/cron command line: a goal can
contain spaces, quotes, newlines, and getting nested command-line
quoting right (especially on Windows, across CreateProcess/cmd.exe/
Task Scheduler's own /TR parsing) is fragile. A PowerShell here-string
/ bash heredoc written directly by Python -- never re-parsed through a
shell -- sidesteps that whole class of bug; verified with a
deliberately adversarial goal containing quotes, $vars, backticks,
and a semicolon, landing in the script byte-for-byte unescaped.

Verified live end-to-end against the real Windows Task Scheduler
(both via the Python API directly and via the `wells schedule` CLI):
registration, `schtasks /query` confirms the task with correct
MINUTE/15 recurrence, removal, and confirmed-gone via a second query.
A skip-gated live test (`test_live_add_and_remove_schedule_windows`)
keeps this covered in CI on Windows runners; Linux/macOS cron paths
are covered by mocking the actual crontab subprocess calls.
